contexts.title: Cybersecurity threat acceleration and investable demand
contexts.summary: Base pass: quick_map thematic screen traced to a personal prediction logged 2026-07-06. Core judgment: threat acceleration is real and well-evidenced, but the public cyber trade (CIBR/HACK/BUG, CRWD/PANW/ZS/OKTA) has already re-rated meaningfully YTD. Extension pass (2026-07-17, standard depth): explicitly excluded CRWD/OKTA/ZS/CIBR per user request; screened non-human identity, AI-SOC automation, OT/cyber-physical security, SBOM/supply-chain security, post-quantum cryptography and cyber insurance, plus a lagging-proxy screen (VRNS/TENB/QLYS/RPD). Key finding: the most credible early names in each niche sub-sector are private and being acquired by strategic/PE buyers (Cisco, Accenture, Palo Alto Networks, Zurich, Thoma Bravo) before reaching public markets; the public small/mid-caps that remain cheap are cheap mainly because the market judges them as weaker franchises or takeover candidates, not because they were overlooked. VRNS stands out as the one name with a genuine growth/price disconnect worth independent verification; SEALSQ is the one public PQC pure-play but carries a bearish analyst view.
blockingGaps: Several figures (Verizon DBIR detail, Gartner spend forecast, ETF YTD performance) are secondary-sourced, not pulled from primary documents
Palo Alto Networks revenue figure sourced in the base pass ($742M) looks inconsistent with known PANW scale; flagged, not corrected
No consensus/expectations check has been run on leading names or on the lagging-proxy cluster (VRNS/TENB/QLYS/RPD)
VRNS's reported ~167x forward P/E needs independent recalculation before any value framing
No public pure-play identified for non-human identity, OT security, SBOM/supply-chain security, or the fastest-growing cyber-insurance underwriters — recorded as an honest structural gap
